jeevamrit.summary: A fermented cow-dung tonic that feeds soil microbes and keeps the root zone alive!
jeevamrit.how: Mix 10 kg cow dung, 10 L cow urine, 2 kg jaggery, 2 kg pulse flour and a handful of bund soil in water to make 200 L. Ferment in shade for 48 hours. Drench 200 L per acre with irrigation water every 15 days, or spray diluted 1:9 (10%) on leaves in the evening.
jeevamrit.frequency: Every 15 days (soil drench) or every 2 weeks (foliar spray)
jeevamrit.evidence: UHF Nauni (Mandla & Sharma 2023, Indian Farming 73(8)): recipe documented; no controlled trial data on this crop's diseases was found. Treat as preventive/suppressive. The 200 L per acre every 15 days rate is the figure most often quoted by natural-farming trainers (not an official HP dose). A CSK HPKV Palampur wheat trial found 10-20% jeevamrit sprays at 2-week intervals gave the best yield, with 10% statistically similar to 20%. Hill farmers in Kinnaur/Shimla report it helps against fungal diseases (anecdotal, unmeasured). A capsicum nutrition trial at UHF Nauni used it among liquid manures (yield, not disease control).

details.what_it_does: Builds soil microbial life. Traditionally credited with suppressing fungal and bacterial diseases, but this is not quantified.
materials_needed: A handful of undisturbed bund/forest soil
preparation_steps: Mix all ingredients in a 200 L drum and make up to 200 L with water.
Cover with a cloth or gunny bag and keep in shade.
application_steps: Soil: run 200 L per acre into the irrigation water, or drench near the roots, every 15 days.
Foliar: mix 1 part jeevamrit with 9 parts water (10%), strain well and spray in the evening every 2 weeks.
Use soon after it is ready; do not keep it for long.
safety_notes: Do not apply on waterlogged soil.

beejamrit.summary: A cow-dung seed coating that protects young roots from soil germs before they even sprout!
beejamrit.how: Hang 5 kg cow dung in a cloth in 20 L water for up to 12 hours, add lime water, 5 L cow urine and a handful of soil, coat the seeds, dry in shade and sow.
beejamrit.frequency: Once, just before sowing or transplanting
beejamrit.evidence: UHF Nauni (Mandla & Sharma 2023, Indian Farming 73(8)): recipe documented; no controlled trial data on this crop's diseases was found. Treat as preventive/suppressive. Seed-treatment recipe only; no disease-control numbers.

details.what_it_does: Coats seeds and seedling roots with beneficial microbes before planting.
preparation_steps: Tie the cow dung in a cloth and hang it in 20 L water for up to 12 hours.
Mix 50 g lime in 1 L water and leave overnight.
Squeeze the dung bundle into the water three times.
Add the soil, cow urine and the lime water and stir.
application_steps: Coat seeds (or dip seedling roots) in the mixture.
Dry the seeds in shade and sow the same day.
safety_notes: Do not soak seeds for long.

neemastra.summary: A fermented neem-and-cow-urine spray against sap-suckers and small caterpillars!
neemastra.how: Ferment 5 kg neem twigs and leaves with 10 L cow urine and 2 kg cow dung in 100 L water for 48 hours in shade, stir twice daily, strain, dilute 2 L in 20 L water (10%) and spray.
neemastra.frequency: At first sign of pests; repeat after 7-10 days if they persist
neemastra.evidence: UHF Nauni (Mandla & Sharma 2023, Indian Farming 73(8)): recipe documented; no controlled trial data on this crop's diseases was found. Treat as preventive/suppressive. The UHF article gives no spray dilution. Training material disagrees (one source says use undiluted, another 2 L in 20 L), so start at 10% (2 L in 20 L) and test on a few plants first. TNAU gives a different recipe; do not mix recipes.

details.what_it_does: Repels and reduces whitefly, aphids, jassids, other sucking insects and small caterpillars.
preparation_steps: Mix everything in a drum and cover with a gunny bag in shade for 48 hours.
Stir clockwise for 1 minute morning and evening.
application_steps: Dilute 2 L of strained Neemastra in 20 L water (10%).
Test on 2-3 plants first and check for leaf burn after a day.
Spray both sides of the leaves in early morning or evening, within a couple of days of straining.
safety_notes: Keep away from eyes and children.
Test on a few plants first to check for leaf burn.

agniastra.summary: A hot neem, chilli and garlic brew in cow urine for borers and sucking pests!
agniastra.how: Boil 2 kg crushed neem leaves, 500 g tobacco powder, 500 g green chilli paste and 250 g garlic paste in 20 L cow urine on low flame under a lid, rest 48 hours, strain and spray 3 L in 100 L water (3%).
agniastra.frequency: At first sign of borers or caterpillars; repeat every 7-10 days
agniastra.evidence: UHF Nauni (Mandla & Sharma 2023, Indian Farming 73(8)): recipe documented; no controlled trial data on this crop's diseases was found. Treat as preventive/suppressive. Spray rates reported by trainers: 3 L per 100 L water (3-4 L in some sources), repeated every 7-10 days. A Kullu brinjal-borer thesis tested 5% and found it effective but weaker than the synthetic standard. Start at 3% and test on 2-3 plants first.

details.what_it_does: Used against sucking insects, small caterpillars and pod/fruit borers.
preparation_steps: Mix all ingredients in the cow urine.
Boil on a low flame with the lid on.
Leave 48 hours, stirring morning and evening.
application_steps: Dilute 3 L of strained Agniastra in 100 L water (3%).
Spray the foliage in early morning or evening, avoiding open flowers, and repeat every 7-10 days if needed.
safety_notes: Wear gloves, mask and eye protection: the chilli and tobacco irritate skin and eyes.
Keep out of reach of children and animals.
Tobacco can carry tobacco mosaic virus: on capsicum, chilli, brinjal and tomato prefer Neemastra or Brahmastra, or make it without tobacco, and wash hands well after handling tobacco.

brahmastra.summary: A bitter five-leaf brew in cow urine that tackles sucking pests and caterpillars!
brahmastra.how: Grind 200 g leaves each of 5 bitter or toxic plants (custard apple, castor, papaya, datura, guava...), simmer in 4 L cow urine, cool 48 hours, strain, and spray 2.5-3 L in 200 L water per acre (up to 6-8 L in 200 L for heavy infestation).
brahmastra.frequency: At first sign of pests; repeat every 10-15 days
brahmastra.evidence: UHF Nauni (Mandla & Sharma 2023, Indian Farming 73(8)): recipe documented; no controlled trial data on this crop's diseases was found. Treat as preventive/suppressive. A Kullu brinjal-borer thesis found Brahmastra 5% effective but weaker than the synthetic standard. Other sources use up to 6-8 L per 200 L water per acre (3%), repeated every 10-15 days. TNAU gives a different recipe; do not mix recipes.

details.what_it_does: Used against sucking insects and caterpillars.
materials_needed: 200 g leaf paste each of any 5 plants (custard apple, castor, papaya, mango, guava, datura, duranta...)
preparation_steps: Grind the leaves to a paste.
Mix with the cow urine and heat until it boils.
application_steps: Start with 2.5-3 L in 200 L water per acre (UHF Nauni rate); use up to 6-8 L in 200 L only for heavy infestation.
Spray the foliage in early morning or evening and repeat every 10-15 days.
safety_notes: Datura and castor are poisonous: wear gloves and a mask.
Keep out of reach of children and animals.
